Shipping Phase 2 as a standalone PR ('legitimate gate-out point', line 342) before Phase 3 completes would mean merging to main with the unresolved vulnerability and all 169 unreviewed hotspots still present — this is not highlighted as a security risk of the gate-out path.

There is no requirement to verify the false-positive claim against the actual code pattern (e.g., confirming the publicly-writable-directory concern is a test fixture, not production code) before the MCP call to change_security_hotspot_status. An incorrect FALSE_POSITIVE suppresses the SonarCloud signal permanently.

The overlap analysis in Task 0.3 (line 260-266) identifies a delta set: SonarCloud security issues with no local ESLint rule equivalent. For security hotspots and vulnerabilities in the delta, this means the local commit gate will never catch them — new instances of the same pattern will be committed and only caught by asynchronous SonarCloud analysis. For a 169-item triage where some will be real fixes to trust-boundary code, pre-commit review would be the stronger posture.
